analysis: The PR modifies only docs/reference/configuration.md, and I found no executable code or security-control change. The visible changed ranges are at lines 969, 977-978, 1115 and 1712-1713. The 969 hunk expands the documented `models[].resource_policy_sha256` derivation to include the resident-assistant tail (`qwen27_tensor_assistant_v1`, depth, inventory SHA, verification and evidence). The head text I received was truncated at line 313, so I could not see the head side of those hunks. The base unit shows lines 1712-1713, the Qwen27 TP assistant policy table. This describes `[backend] mtp_mode` and the saved `tensorAssistant` policy, which is refused beside `nativeMember` and serves local clusters only. The base text does not change the stated security properties: the assistant is not offered to the coordinator, speculative decoding has no parity qualification, and the native worker is bilaterally bound at LOAD. Because the head side of 1712-1713 was not visible, I cannot confirm whether the new wording weakens or contradicts those claims (for example, whether it now implies public or coordinator-served speculative decoding without qualification). The documentation does not appear to change TB-011/T-054 build-qualification posture, and no endpoints, environment variables or defaults are added in the visible portions. The prefix cache documentation (lines 62-67) is unchanged and consistent with T-041: default-on, with `DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0` as the kill switch. Remaining question for integration: confirm that the hunks at 977-978 and 1115 (which fall outside the supplied text, base starts at 1475 and head ends at 313) and the head side of 1712-1713 do not overclaim public or serving grants for the Qwen27 assistant or the pair_serving_grant evidence. No finding is reportable on the supplied evidence.
